# Jubilees Chapter 49 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

## 49:2 — "powers of Mastema had been let loose"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "all the powers of Mastema had been let loose" | Literal; "let loose" captures the Ge'ez release verb |
| LOGOS | "all the powers of Mastema had been let loose" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "Mastema's full force had been unleashed" | Dynamic; "unleashed" is vivid equivalent |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted EMET/LOGOS "let loose." The Ge'ez verb is specific about the release of previously restrained powers. "Unleashed" (PNEUMA) is a good dynamic equivalent but the formal "let loose" preserves the Ge'ez restraint-then-release structure.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 49:8 — timing calculation

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "from the third part of the day to the third part of the night" | Literal |
| LOGOS | "from the third part of the day to the third part of the night; for two portions of the day are given to the light and one third to the evening" | Adds the explanatory clause present in Ge'ez |
| PNEUMA | "starting from a third of the way through the day, running through a third of the night" | Simplifies |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS — the explanatory clause "for two portions of the day are given to the light and one third to the evening" is in the Ge'ez and is important for understanding the timing calculation. PNEUMA drops this.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 49:11 — "wine — the blood of the grape"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "ye shall drink wine and blood of the grape" | Literal; possibly hendiadys |
| LOGOS | "you shall drink wine — the blood of the grape" | Em dash clarifies as appositive |
| PNEUMA | "Drink wine — the blood of the grape" | Same as LOGOS |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS "wine — the blood of the grape." The Ge'ez uses two terms in apposition: "wine" and "blood of the grape" are the same thing, not two separate drinks. EMET's "and" suggests two items.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS/PNEUMA.

---
